notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 07/13/2025
Patient: Sophie Lubowitz, 64-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 07/13/2025. The study assessed sleep patterns and breathing abnormalities throughout the night. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 18.5 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 6% of all events. Oxygen saturation levels showed mild intermittent desaturation corresponding to respiratory events. Sleep architecture was within normal limits with expected distribution of sleep stages.

In summary, the findings indicate moderate sleep apnea with a small proportion of central and mixed apneas. Clinical correlation and consideration of treatment options are advised.

notes.title: Sleep Medicine Consultation
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/09/2026
Patient: Sophie Lubowitz, 65-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of obstructive sleep apnea with CPAP therapy.

History:
Ms. Lubowitz has a history of obstructive sleep apnea and has been using CPAP therapy. She reports consistent nightly use of her CPAP device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 32.4 kg/m2.

Assessment:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 27.3 events/hour on CPAP at 12 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options given CPAP failure.
2. Discuss potential for advanced therapies or referral for further evaluation.
3. Continue monitoring symptoms and adherence.
4. Schedule follow-up appointment in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Summary:
Ms. Lubowitz demonstrates persistent obstructive events despite adherence to CPAP therapy at adequate pressure settings. Further management strategies will be explored to improve her sleep quality and reduce apnea events.

Otolaryngology Consultation Note

Oropharynx: tonsils size 1, no other anatomic obstruction. No neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal palsy, severe cardiopulmonary disease or planned MRI; able to operate the sleep remote.

Based on these findings, the patient appears to be an appropriate candidate for hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy. Further steps will include device implantation planning and patient education regarding device use and follow-up care.
